response: ["When melanoma is suspected, the whole lesion should be completely excised with a narrow (1-3 mm) margin to perform histological diagnosis.", "Incisional biopsies can be performed on large lesions such as lesions on the face (e.g., lentigo maligna), acral lesions, and on the genitalia.", "The consensus rate for the recommendation is 100 % (21 out of 21).", "Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is the recommended and first‑line treatment for primary cutaneous melanoma of any thickness.", "Surgical excision with histologically negative margins is also the recommended and first‑line treatment for melanoma in situ.", "Surgical margins should be based on tumor thickness.", "Sentinel lymph node biopsy, when indicated, should be performed before wide excision of the primary tumor.", "Sentinel lymph node biopsy should be performed in the same operative setting as wide excision whenever possible.", "The 6‑point score is driven by the presence of a blue‑whitish veil, irregular streaks, localized irregular pigmentation, irregular dots and globules, and regression structures.", "A blue‑whitish veil contributes 2 points when present.", "Each of the following contributes 1 point when present: irregular streaks, localized irregular pigmentation, irregular dots and globules, and regression structures.", "Pigment network contributes 0 points when typical, and vascular structures contribute 0 points when absent."]
